newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Argentina to reduce tax on Brazil soluble coffee.
newsitem.headline: Argentina to reduce tax on Brazil soluble coffee.

text.p: Argentine government officials have agreed to reduce to zero an import tax on Brazilian soluble coffee, said a Brazilian government official.
"The idea is to reduce the tax to zero," said Mauricio Assis, head of the primary commodities department at Brazil's Industry and Commerce Ministry.
The tax which stood at 18 percent last year was cut to 12 percent at the beginning of 1997, according to Mauro Malta, executive secretary of Brazil's Soluble Coffee Industry Association.
Assis said he did not know exactly when the tax would be reduced but Malta said he understand the cut would take place within the next month.
Sales of Brazilian soluble coffee to Argentina are very small however.

Of the 58,000 tonnes exported by Brazil last year, only 433 tonnes went to Argentina. This could rise to 650 tonnes with a zero tax, Malta said. ((-Caroline Bulloch, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 5074151))
